scope: Original presentation asset replacing the industrial delivery cart, rails and winch; no canonical rule or quantity changes.
date_location: A reconstructed lighter straight-box trail wagon, western United States, approximately1865-1880. Not a replica of a named surviving wagon or the enormous Montana heavy-freight variant.

sources.title: NPS, Wagons on the Emigrant Trails
sources.claim: Murphy straight box, approximately12ft bed and9ft overall height; ox teams; wheels, running gear and cover. The pictured wagon is a1979 reconstruction, used for construction relationships, not as a period photograph.

sources.title: Kennedy, Whoop-Up Trail documentation, NPS/Montana SHPO,1991
sources.claim: Murphy red running gear, blue box and white top. The following dimensions describe a much larger heavy-freight variant and are not borrowed for this lighter wagon.
sources.consulted: Relevant text re-read; cited background Madsen and Madsen1980 p50 not independently consulted.

sources.title: NPS, Transportation on the Santa Fe Trail
sources.claim: Wagon types varied; undated loading-dock photograph shows open bows, wooden boxes, large spoked rear wheels and smaller front wheels. Exact paint cannot be inferred from this monochrome picture.
sources.consulted: Article and actual loading-dock photograph reviewed.

sources.title: Ford and Kreutzer, Oxen: Engines of Overland Emigration, Overland Journal, Spring2015, hosted by NPS
sources.claim: Wooden neck beam, loose wooden U-bows and pins; separate tongue and calabash rings. A chain pulls the wagon; the tongue steers and restrains it. Longhorns with trimmed horns suited the lead, while heavier cattle worked by the wagon.
sources.consulted: Text and yoke photograph inspected. This modern technical/historical interpretation does not authenticate an exact nineteenth-century museum object.

sources.title: Muybridge, Ox, walking, c1881, Library of Congress
sources.claim: A period sequential photographic reference for a grounded ox walk, distinct from the existing stampede run.
sources.consulted: Catalogue metadata and actual nine-image plate reviewed.

render_brief.body: Straight wooden bed3.66m long and1.12m wide; blue exterior plank box, unpainted inner loading floor, red wooden bolsters, reach, axles, spokes, hubs and felloes; dark iron tires and fasteners. No engine, winch, metal rails, rubber tires, modern lights, suspension springs, logos or invented manufacturer lettering.
render_brief.wheels: Separate front and rear wheels, with smaller front wheels. Reconstructed diameters1.10m front and1.40m rear;12 front and14 rear spokes. These dimensions and spoke counts are modelling choices, not measured period Murphy specifications.
render_brief.cover: White canvas over six bent wooden bows, overall height2.74m. Canvas drawn to the front portion to show the cargo is reconstructed loading-stage arrangement; the period photograph supports uncovered bows, not this exact fold pattern.
render_brief.hardware: Separate tongue and chain attachment; no misleading claim that oxen pull by the tongue. Basic iron bands, axle stubs, front pivot and its wooden axle bed are reconstructed functional fittings. Mirrored shallow wheel dish is a functional reconstruction, not a measured Murphy specification. In v004 the chain fitting hangs from a solid timber under the front box, as W4 describes. Its reconstructed height is chosen above the tongue so the chain does not pass through wood. No elaborate unsupported brake system.
render_brief.colour: Documented red/blue/white rendered at full natural strength. Numeric paint colours are reconstructed; no faded or deliberately muted treatment. The v002 review uses a neutral Standard view transform and warm lighting to retain the saturated paint colours.
render_brief.people: No new person is included in the static wagon asset.
render_brief.team: An ox team requires its own source/appearance/motion review. Do not directly reuse the untrimmed stampede longhorn as a wheeler: W4 contradicts that choice. Preserve all approved stampede geometry and clips. No self-propelled empty wagon.
render_brief.game_scale: Source dimensions in metres. Any uniform miniature scale for the battle diorama will be explicitly recorded at integration. Cargo quantities still represent public rule output; they do not assert literal freight weights.

history_lines: Trail wagons carried goods in wooden boxes.
Oxen pulled through chains; tongues steered.
This lighter wagon's exact fittings are rebuilt.
required_review: Actual source views of wheels, running gear, box and canopy
Separate sourced oxen, yokes and grounded walk
Native cargo quantity and Native plain-crate filtering
Both directions, terrain, fuse clearance, skip and cleanup
Optional sourced history and final package
